summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She had been on home TPN due to inability to tolerate oral intake. Initial labs showed normal lipase and LFTs, and a CT scan revealed no acute findings. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, TPN, and IV pain and nausea control. An endoscopy was performed to rule out gastritis or ulcers, which showed normal findings. Her pain and nausea gradually improved, allowing transition to oral medications and advancement to a soft diet. Platelet count, which had been low, normalized by discharge. She was discharged home with continued TPN, oral pain and nausea medications, new constipation regimen, and follow-up plans with gastroenterology and her therapist.
